subject: Human Evolution
title: Olduvai Gorge
description: Learn Olduvai Gorge in one minute.

hook.text: A 50-km gash in Tanzania's Serengeti exposes two million years of sediment—and human history.

buildup.text: Olduvai Gorge's layered walls act like a timeline: deeper layers hold older tools and bones.

discovery.text: The gorge yielded the oldest known stone tools—simple Oldowan choppers dating to 1.8 million years.

twist.text: Multiple hominin species lived here at the same time, competing for the same resources.

climax.text: Olduvai became paleoanthropology's most famous address: where the human story literally reads from the walls.

punchline.text: A gorge that opens a window into deep time.

quiz.question: Why is Olduvai Gorge important for human evolution?
options: It has the oldest cave art
Layered sediments expose 2 million years of fossils
